title: Parmigiana di Melanzane
subtitle: Baked aubergine with tomato, mozzarella, and parmesan
excerpt: Parmigiana di melanzane is layered fried aubergine, tomato sauce, mozzarella, and parmesan baked until bubbling and deeply browned on top. It is one of the great Italian vegetable dishes: rich, satisfying, and just as good the day after it is made.
sourceNotes: Parmigiana di melanzane is claimed by both Naples and Sicily, and the argument over its origin has never been settled. The name does not refer to the city of Parma but may derive from the Sicilian word 'parmiciana', meaning overlapping slats. The dish appears in Ippolito Cavalcanti's Cucina Teorico-Pratica (1837) and Pellegrino Artusi's La Scienza in Cucina e l'Arte di Mangiar Bene (1891), establishing it as a 19th-century classic.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions after baking. Reheat from frozen at 180°C for 30 to 35 minutes covered in foil, then uncovered for 10 more minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the day before. It is much better after a night in the fridge, reheated the next day. Serve warm, not piping hot.

content.text: Parmigiana di melanzane is one of Italy's great vegetable dishes. Thin slices of aubergine are salted, fried until golden, then layered with tomato sauce, mozzarella, and parmesan in a baking dish. It goes in the oven for about an hour and comes out deeply browned, bubbling, and smelling of cooked tomato and cheese. It is better the day after it is made, once the layers have had time to settle.

items.prepNote: 1 for salting the aubergine, 1 for the sauce

content.text: Lay the aubergine slices in a colander, salting each layer. Leave for 30 minutes. Rinse and pat thoroughly dry.
Fry the aubergine in batches in a generous layer of olive oil over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden. Drain on kitchen paper.
Fry the garlic in 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes, crush them, and cook for 20 minutes until thick. Season with salt.

Heat the oven to 190°C. Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce over the base of the baking dish. Lay a layer of aubergine slices over the sauce. Add mozzarella slices, basil leaves, a sprinkle of parmesan, and another spoon of sauce. Repeat until all the ingredients are used, finishing with a layer of sauce and a generous scatter of parmesan.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes until deeply browned on top and bubbling around the edges. Leave to rest for at least 30 minutes before cutting. Serve warm.

The parmigiana argument between Naples and Sicily has never been resolved. Neapolitans claim it as their own; Sicilians point to the name, which may derive from a Sicilian word for overlapping slats. The earliest documented recipe is Neapolitan. Regardless of origin, the dish is eaten throughout southern Italy in summer when aubergines are cheapest and best.
